questions.q: What is Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD), now called Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense?

choices.text: Unified software that combines ASA features, legacy FirePOWER Services, and new features
choices.why: Correct. FTD is the unified image that merges ASA firewall functions with FirePOWER (Sourcefire) services and newer capabilities.

choices.text: The on-box web manager used to configure a single small firewall
choices.why: That describes Firepower Device Manager (FDM), which manages FTD locally; it is not the firewall software itself.

choices.text: The operating system on Firepower chassis that controls basic device operations
choices.why: That is FXOS (Firepower eXtensible Operating System). FTD runs as a logical device on top of the chassis, not as the chassis OS.

choices.text: A hardware module that brought Sourcefire technology into the ASA
choices.why: That is the Cisco ASA FirePOWER module. FTD is a unified software image, not an add-on module.

questions.q: An administrator enters the nameif inside command on an ASA interface without specifying a security level. What security level does the interface receive by default?

choices.why: Security level 0 is the default for any interface name other than "inside", such as outside or dmz.
Correct. nameif assigns security level 100 to an interface named "inside" and 0 to any other name.
50 is a common manual choice for a DMZ, but nameif never assigns it by default; a DMZ level must be set by hand.

choices.text: No level, so it does not pass traffic
choices.why: An interface named "inside" automatically gets level 100. An interface with no security level would not respond at the network layer, but that is not the case here.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: An engineer has two ASA interfaces that are both configured with security level 50. Hosts on these interfaces cannot communicate with each other. Which command allows this traffic?

choices.why: access-group applies an ACL to an interface; by itself it does not lift the ASA's default restriction on traffic between equal security levels.
nameif names the interface and sets a default level of 100; it does not permit traffic between interfaces with the same level.
Correct. This global command allows traffic between interfaces that share the same security level.
service-policy activates an MPF policy map for inspection or QoS; it does not control same-security-level traffic.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: In a Cisco IOS Zone-Based Firewall, how is traffic destined to the router itself handled by default?

choices.text: It is dropped until a zone pair policy permits it
choices.why: That is the behavior for traffic between two different zones. The self zone is the exception to the deny-all rule.

choices.text: It is passed only if CBAC is also enabled
choices.why: CBAC is the legacy IOS firewall that ZBFW replaced; it plays no role in how the self zone behaves.

choices.text: It is inspected and logged before being dropped
choices.why: Inspect is an action applied by a zone pair policy, and it does not result in a drop. Self zone traffic is allowed by default.

choices.text: It is allowed until it is explicitly denied
choices.why: Correct. The self zone is the only exception to the ZBFW deny-all behavior: traffic to the router is allowed until explicitly denied.

questions.section: 2. Comparing Network Security Solutions That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: When a Cisco ASA or Secure Firewall is deployed in transparent mode, which interface holds the IP address used for the bridged segment?

choices.why: The cluster control link carries control and data traffic between cluster members; it has nothing to do with transparent mode addressing.
Correct. In transparent mode the bridged pair of interfaces has no addresses of its own; the BVI holds the IP address.
In transparent mode the inside and outside interfaces are bridged and carry no IP addresses.
The failover link is used by an HA pair to check each other's status, not to address a transparent bridge group.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: Which failover mode is the only one supported by Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense?

choices.why: Correct. Secure Firewall supports only Active-Standby failover, where one unit passes traffic and the other waits.
Active-Active failover, where both units pass traffic, is supported on the ASA only, not on Secure Firewall.
Clustering groups several units into one logical device; it is a different feature from failover, not a failover mode.
Fail-open lets traffic bypass a failed inline device. It is an interface option, not a high availability failover mode.

questions.q: A Secure Firewall unit boots and looks for a cluster master over the cluster control link, but none responds. What happens next?

choices.text: It becomes a slave and waits for a master to appear
choices.why: A unit becomes a slave only when a master already exists. With no master present, it takes the master role itself.

choices.text: It moves immediately to the disabled state
choices.why: The disabled state follows a configuration sync or health failure, not the absence of a master.

choices.text: It stays in the On-Call state until an administrator intervenes
choices.why: On-Call is a state a unit can be in while the master admits units one at a time; it is not the result of finding no master.

choices.text: It waits 45 seconds and then becomes the master
choices.why: Correct. A booting unit that finds no master waits 45 seconds and then becomes the master.

questions.q: In what order does a Cisco ASA evaluate access rules for a packet arriving on an interface?

choices.text: Global ACL, then interface ACL, then implicit deny
choices.why: The order is reversed here. The interface ACL is checked before the global ACL.

choices.text: Implicit deny, then interface ACL, then global ACL
choices.why: The implicit deny is always last; if it came first, nothing would ever be permitted.

choices.text: Interface ACL, then global ACL, then implicit deny
choices.why: Correct. The ASA checks the interface ACL first, then the global ACL, and finally the implicit deny.

choices.text: Interface ACL, then implicit deny, then global ACL
choices.why: The global ACL is evaluated before the implicit deny; otherwise the global ACL could never match.

questions.q: Which syslog message ID does a Cisco ASA generate when the implicit deny at the end of an ACL drops a packet?

choices.why: Correct. Syslog message 106023 is generated when the implicit deny drops a packet.
2385 is the RFC number for BGP MD5 authentication, not a syslog message ID.
8305 is the TCP port of the FMC to managed device management tunnel (sftunnel), not a syslog ID.
IEC 61850 is the Ethernet-based protocol for electrical substation automation, not an ASA syslog message.

questions.q: An engineer is configuring ASA application inspection with the Modular Policy Framework. What is the first step?

choices.text: Activate the service policy globally or on an interface
choices.why: Activating the service policy with the service-policy command is the last of the three steps, not the first.

choices.text: Associate actions with each class to create a policy map
choices.why: Associating actions with classes is the second step; the classes must exist first.

choices.text: Enable TCP sequence number randomization on the outside interface
choices.why: Sequence randomization is a NAT-related protection, not part of configuring application inspection.

choices.text: Configure traffic classes to identify interesting traffic
choices.why: Correct. First you configure traffic classes (class maps), then associate actions to create service policies, then activate them.

questions.q: A company has one public IP address, 209.165.200.229. Web traffic on TCP 80 must reach 192.168.10.10, and email on TCP 25 must reach 192.168.10.20. Which translation method should be used?

choices.why: Dynamic NAT maps hosts one-to-one from a pool of global addresses for outbound traffic; it does not send different ports on one IP to different servers.
Correct. Static PAT maps different ports on one global IP to different inside servers, as in this example.
Identity NAT keeps the address the same and bypasses translation, so it cannot redirect ports to inside servers.
Dynamic PAT lets many inside hosts share one global IP for outbound connections; it does not provide fixed inbound port mappings.

questions.q: Two routers form a BGP peering with MD5 authentication through a Cisco ASA, but the session keeps failing. Which ASA behavior is the most likely cause?

choices.text: Application inspection rewriting embedded IP addresses
choices.why: Application inspection handles embedded addresses for protocols such as TFTP; it is not what breaks the BGP MD5 hash.

choices.text: The implicit deny dropping UDP 123 traffic
choices.why: UDP 123 is NTP. Blocking it affects time sync, but BGP runs over TCP and the MD5 failure comes from changed sequence numbers.
Correct. The ASA randomizes TCP sequence numbers, which changes the TCP header that BGP MD5 (RFC 2385) hashes, so it must be turned off for this peering.

choices.text: Dynamic PAT changing the source port to 1024
choices.why: BGP peers are normally not behind PAT, and the documented problem is sequence randomization breaking the MD5 hash check.

questions.q: Which Talos base intrusion policy is designed to balance performance and security and is the right choice for most networks?

choices.why: Correct. This base policy balances performance and security and suits most networks.
Connectivity Over Security has far fewer rules and only the most critical blocking rules, for networks you are fairly confident in.
Security Over Connectivity puts security before convenience with many anomaly rules, meant for high-risk traffic.
Maximum Detection puts even more emphasis on security with more operational impact; it is not the general-purpose choice.

questions.q: In Secure Firewall intrusion rules, which system default variable represents the inside, protected network?

choices.why: $EXTERNAL_NET represents the outside, unprotected network.
$HTTP_SERVERS identifies the web servers, not the whole protected network.
Correct. $HOME_NET is the variable for the inside, protected network.
$DNS_SERVERS identifies DNS servers only, not the protected network as a whole.

questions.q: Which Secure Firewall preprocessor monitors the handshake of encrypted sessions and then stops inspecting once the traffic is encrypted, reducing false positives?

choices.why: The SSH preprocessor detects buffer overflow attempts and illegal SSH versions; it does not watch SSL handshakes.
The HTTP preprocessor normalizes requests and responses and detects URI-encoding attacks in cleartext HTTP.
The DCE/RPC preprocessor watches DCE/RPC and SMB traffic for anomalies and evasions.
Correct. The SSL preprocessor monitors the handshake, stops once the session is encrypted, needs TCP stream preprocessing, and reduces false positives.

questions.q: Which Cisco Secure Malware Defense engine uses machine learning and active heuristics on execution attributes to find previously unknown threats?

choices.why: Ethos is the fuzzy fingerprinting engine that uses static or passive heuristics to match polymorphic variants.
Correct. Spero is the machine-learning engine that uses active heuristics on execution attributes to identify unknown malware.
1-to-1 signatures compare a file hash against a database; any change to the file evades them, so they don't find unknown threats.
Device flow correlation gives a kernel-level view of network I/O traced back to the process; it is not a machine-learning file classifier.

questions.q: A file was given a clean disposition when it entered the network. A week later, Cisco's cloud reclassifies it as malicious. What does Secure Malware Defense do?

choices.text: Nothing, because the file already passed inspection
choices.why: Point-in-time systems would do nothing, but Secure Malware Defense goes beyond point-in-time detection with retrospection.

choices.text: It tells every connector that saw the file to quarantine it
choices.why: Correct. Retrospection tracks even clean files, and if one turns malicious, every connector that saw it is told to quarantine it.

choices.text: It adds the file hash to the Security Intelligence allowlist
choices.why: An allowlist exempts traffic from the blocklist, which is the opposite of what is needed for a malicious file.

choices.text: It schedules an SRU to deploy a new Snort rule
choices.why: SRUs deliver Snort rule sets on a schedule; retrospective alerts and quarantine come from Secure Malware Defense, not an SRU.

questions.q: By default, how often does Secure Firewall update Security Intelligence feeds?

choices.why: 5 minutes is the minimum interval you can set for the Talos network feed, not the default.
30 minutes is the minimum interval for the Talos URL and DNS feed and for custom feeds, not the default.
Weekly is the schedule for geolocation updates, not Security Intelligence feeds.
Correct. Security Intelligence feeds update every 2 hours by default, and the interval can be lowered for more agile blocklisting.

questions.section: 8. Security Intelligence, Security Updates, and Keeping Firepower Software Up to Date

questions.q: On which schedule does Cisco normally release Snort rule updates (SRUs)?

choices.text: Tuesday and Thursday, plus out-of-band for critical updates
choices.why: Correct. SRUs are released on Tuesday and Thursday, with out-of-band releases for critical updates.

choices.text: Weekly, on the same schedule as geolocation updates
choices.why: Geolocation updates are the ones released weekly; SRUs come twice a week.

choices.text: Every 2 hours, like Security Intelligence feeds
choices.why: Every 2 hours is the default Security Intelligence feed update interval, not the SRU schedule.

choices.text: Only when a new VDB version is published
choices.why: The VDB is a separate update type with known vulnerabilities; SRUs follow their own regular schedule.

questions.section: 8. Security Intelligence, Security Updates, and Keeping Firepower Software Up to Date

questions.q: A manufacturing company needs a rugged firewall that can see and control industrial protocols such as Modbus and DNP3 in its OT network. Which product fits best?

choices.why: Cloud Native is a Kubernetes-based firewall for cloud-native applications, not a rugged appliance for OT networks.

choices.text: Cisco Secure WAF and bot protection
choices.why: Secure WAF protects websites and APIs against attacks such as SQL injection and bots, not industrial control traffic.
Correct. The ISA3000 is a rugged industrial security appliance that supports DNP3, CIP, Modbus, and IEC 61850.
The 9300 Series targets service providers and high-performance data centers, not rugged industrial environments.

questions.q: Which company originally created the Snort open-source IPS engine and whose technology became Cisco FirePOWER?

choices.why: WheelGroup is the company Cisco bought that introduced the legacy Cisco IDS and IPS systems, not Snort.
ThreatGRID was acquired for malware analysis and sandboxing, which became Cisco Secure Malware Analytics.
Correct. Sourcefire created Snort, and its technology became Cisco FirePOWER.
Immunet is an antivirus community that feeds intelligence into the Malware Analytics cloud; it did not create Snort.

questions.q: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) was previously known by which names?

choices.text: Firepower Device Manager and Adaptive Security Device Manager
choices.why: FDM is the on-box FTD manager and ASDM is the ASA GUI manager; both are separate products from the FMC.

choices.text: Firepower Management Center and FireSIGHT Management Center
choices.why: Correct. The FMC was formerly Firepower Management Center and, before that, FireSIGHT Management Center.

choices.text: Cisco Defense Orchestrator and Firepower Chassis Manager
choices.why: CDO is a cloud-based manager and FCM is the FXOS web GUI; neither is a former FMC name.
Those names belong to Cisco's XDR and incident response tools, not the firewall management center.

questions.q: An engineer needs to register an FTD device with the FMC, but the device sits behind a PAT device and its IP address is unknown. What should the engineer enter in the FMC?

choices.text: Only the device's IP address, leaving the registration key blank
choices.why: The registration key is always required, and here the IP address is the value that is unknown.

choices.text: The device's IP address and a platform settings policy
choices.why: A platform settings policy shares parameters like time and external authentication; it does not authenticate registration.

choices.text: A variable set and the cluster control link address
choices.why: Variable sets pair with intrusion policies and the cluster control link is for clustering; neither is used to register a device.

choices.text: The NAT ID and registration key, leaving the IP address blank
choices.why: Correct. When the IP is unknown or behind NAT or PAT, you enter only a unique NAT ID and the registration key.

questions.q: Which Firepower platform does not support the Firepower Chassis Manager (FCM) web GUI and offers only the FXOS CLI?

choices.why: Correct. FCM is not available on the Firepower 2100 series, which has only the FXOS CLI.
The Firepower 9300 is a chassis with modules running logical devices, configured with FCM or the FXOS CLI.
The 4100 series is a chassis platform that supports FCM and clustering.
The ASA 5508-X is not a Firepower chassis; it runs ASA software or FTD natively and is managed with tools such as ASDM, FDM, or the FMC.

questions.q: A university wants to keep student and faculty networks on one physical ASA, with separate policies, routing tables, and administrators for each. Which feature should it use?

choices.why: Inline sets group inline pairs for IPS inspection; they do not create separate firewalls with their own administrators.
Object grouping reduces the number of viewable ACEs; it does not partition the appliance.
Correct. Security contexts in multiple context mode partition one ASA into virtual firewalls with their own configuration, policies, routing, and administrators.
Clustering joins several units into one logical device for throughput and redundancy, the opposite of partitioning one device.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: In ASA multiple context mode, which context gives the device network access to resources such as AAA and syslog servers?

choices.why: The system execution space manages the whole device but relies on the admin context for network access.
Correct. The admin context provides network access to resources such as AAA and syslog servers, and sends syslogs and SNMP traps for the system.
A user (customer) context is a regular virtual firewall for a tenant, not the one that serves the system's management needs.
The self zone is a ZBFW concept for traffic to the router itself, not an ASA context.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: In multiple context mode, contexts share an interface. How does the ASA packet classifier decide which context should process an incoming packet?

choices.text: By the destination IP address or a unique MAC address
choices.why: Correct. With shared interfaces, the classifier uses a unique MAC address or the destination IP address, relying on each context's NAT table.

choices.text: By looking up the destination in the routing table
choices.why: The classifier can't use routing tables, because contexts can have overlapping networks.

choices.text: By the source port of the packet
choices.why: Source ports are not used for classification; classification is by interface, MAC address, or destination IP.

choices.text: By the security level of the ingress interface
choices.why: Security levels control trust between interfaces; they are not how the classifier chooses a context.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: An FTD is deployed as an inline pair. The business requires that traffic keep flowing even if the device loses power or its software fails. Which setting provides this?

choices.text: Passive mode with a SPAN port
choices.why: Passive mode only inspects a copy of the traffic and doesn't prevent attacks, so it does not meet the inline requirement.
A state link passes connection state between an HA pair; it does not let traffic bypass a single failed inline device.
Inline normalization is a network preprocessor setting that prevents evasion; it does not keep traffic flowing on failure.
Correct. Fail-open lets traffic bypass an inline device's rules and policies when it fails. Without it, all traffic is dropped.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: Which Secure Firewall interface mode receives packets through a GRE tunnel from a remote capture point and is supported only in routed mode?

choices.why: Inline pair with tap bridges two physical interfaces and inspects a copy of traffic; it is supported in routed or transparent mode.
Correct. Passive with ERSPAN uses one interface as a sniffer that receives packets through a GRE tunnel, and it is supported only in routed mode.
Switched mode bridges interfaces under a BVI; it does not receive traffic from a remote GRE tunnel.
An inline set sits physically in the traffic path; it does not receive mirrored traffic over GRE.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: Which of the following is carried over the dedicated failover link between two units in a high availability pair?

choices.text: Hello messages (keepalives) and MAC address exchange
choices.why: Correct. The failover link carries firewall state, hello keepalives, network link status, MAC address exchange, and configuration replication.

choices.text: Forwarded data packets for centralized features
choices.why: Forwarded data packets travel over a cluster control link in clustering, not over a failover link.
Security Intelligence feeds are downloaded from Cisco or custom sources, not exchanged over the failover link.

choices.text: ERSPAN traffic from a remote switch
choices.why: ERSPAN traffic arrives on a passive sniffer interface through GRE; failover interfaces can be used only for failover.

questions.q: An engineer wants to pair two FTD devices for failover, but the FMC refuses. One device gets its outside address from the ISP by DHCP. What is the problem?

choices.text: The devices are in transparent mode
choices.why: Transparent mode is fine as long as both units use the same firewall mode.

choices.text: Failover requires a subinterface for the failover link
choices.why: The reverse is true: subinterfaces are not supported for failover links.

choices.text: DHCP and PPPoE are not allowed on any interface of a failover pair
choices.why: Correct. Failover requires that no interface uses DHCP or PPPoE, along with matching mode, software, NTP, and licenses.

choices.text: The devices need different software versions for failover
choices.why: Failover requires the same software version on both devices, not different versions.

questions.q: What is the default cluster control link on a Secure Firewall cluster?

choices.why: Gigabit Ethernet 1 is used in the book's failover example; it is not the default cluster control link.
Cisco says to keep the management network separate from the cluster control link.
A BVI holds the IP address for a bridge group in transparent mode; it is not a cluster link.
Correct. The cluster control link is Port-channel 48 by default.

questions.q: Which ASA ACL type filters on the Ethernet type code in the Layer 2 header and can be used only in transparent mode?

choices.why: A Webtype ACL restricts traffic that comes through SSL VPN tunnels.
Correct. An EtherType ACL filters on the Ethernet type code, such as 0x800 for IP, and works only in transparent mode.
A standard ACL matches only destination IP addresses, is used by processes such as route maps, and works only in routed mode.
An extended ACL matches IPs, protocols, ports, ICMP types, and users; it works in both routed and transparent mode.

questions.q: A consultant needs network access from March 1 to March 31 only. Which time range type should be applied to the ACL?

choices.why: Correct. An absolute time range has a start and end time, which suits a fixed consulting engagement. Only one is allowed per time range.
Periodic time ranges recur, such as weekday business hours; they don't define a single start and end date.
weekend is a periodic keyword meaning Saturday and Sunday, not a fixed date range.
A downloadable ACL is an advanced ASA filtering feature, not a time range type.

questions.q: An administrator wants to stop ICMP echo requests from any source to the ASA's outside interface while still allowing other ICMP types. Which pair of commands does this?

choices.text: access-list outside_in deny icmp any any echo, then access-group outside_in in interface outside
choices.why: An interface ACL filters through-the-box ICMP; by default it does not block ICMP sent to the ASA's own interface.

choices.text: icmp permit any outside, then icmp deny any echo outside
choices.why: ICMP commands are processed in order, so the permit-all would match echo first and the deny would never be reached.

choices.text: icmp deny any echo outside, then icmp permit any outside
choices.why: Correct. The ICMP policy is processed in order: the first line blocks echo to the outside interface and the second permits all other ICMP types.

choices.text: same-security-traffic permit inter-interface, then icmp deny any outside
choices.why: The first command allows traffic between same-level interfaces, and the second would block all ICMP rather than only echo.

questions.q: Which address translation deployment lets many inside hosts share one global IP address and is described as the most common deployment?

choices.why: Static NAT is a fixed one-to-one translation, so 100 hosts would need 100 global addresses.
Dynamic NAT maps hosts one-to-one from a pool, so the pool needs as many addresses as hosts.
Identity NAT bypasses translation and keeps the address the same.
Correct. Dynamic PAT lets many inside hosts share one global IP using source ports, and it is the most common deployment.

questions.q: How does Secure Firewall process the rules in an access control policy?

choices.text: Top-down by ascending number, and the first matching rule handles the traffic, except for Monitor rules
choices.why: Correct. Rules are evaluated in order from rule 1, and the first match wins, except Monitor rules, which log and let evaluation continue.

choices.text: The most specific rule wins regardless of its position
choices.why: Secure Firewall does not use best-match logic; the order you set decides which rule handles the traffic.

choices.text: Rules are grouped by category, and categories change rule priority
choices.why: Sections and categories are only organizational and don't change rule position.

choices.text: Block rules are always evaluated before allow rules
choices.why: The action does not change evaluation order; rules are evaluated strictly top-down by number.

questions.q: Which Talos base policy enables malware, exploit kit, old and common vulnerability, and known in-the-wild exploit rules, and has the most operational impact?

choices.why: Security Over Connectivity is strict with many anomaly rules, but Maximum Detection goes further and has more operational impact.
Correct. Maximum Detection puts even more emphasis on security, enables those rule categories, and requires checking that legitimate traffic isn't dropped.
No Rules Active has no active rules at all, so it enables nothing.
Balanced Security and Connectivity balances performance and security and is right for most networks.

questions.q: What does the Secure Firewall vulnerability database (VDB) contain, and how is it used?

choices.text: The latest Snort rules, released twice a week
choices.why: That describes an SRU (Snort rule update), not the VDB.

choices.text: Reputation lists of IPs, URLs, and domains to block early
choices.why: That describes Security Intelligence feeds, which block by reputation before deeper inspection.

choices.text: Known vulnerabilities identified by CVE, used to set the impact of intrusion events
choices.why: Correct. The VDB holds known vulnerabilities identified by CVE and is used to set the impact level of intrusion events.

choices.text: IP address to country mappings, updated weekly
choices.why: That describes geolocation updates, which are released weekly.

questions.q: Which standard defines a format for threat intelligence such as C2 addresses, domains, and malware hashes, and was developed by MITRE and is now maintained by OASIS?

choices.why: TAXII is also from MITRE and OASIS, but it is the transport for exchanging threat information, not the format.
CVE identifies known vulnerabilities; it is not a format for threat intelligence like C2 addresses and hashes.
SIEM is a type of platform that aggregates and analyzes event data, not a threat intelligence format.
Correct. STIX (Structured Threat Information eXpression) is the standard format for threat intelligence, developed by MITRE and maintained by OASIS.

questions.q: Which product was Cisco's first, now legacy, firewall?

choices.why: PIX (Private Internet Exchange) was a popular Cisco firewall that came through acquisitions and preceded the ASA, but it was not the first.
Correct. Centri Firewall was Cisco's first firewall, now legacy.
The ASA was released in the early 2000s, well after Cisco's first firewall.
ZBFW is a router-based firewall that replaced CBAC; it was not Cisco's first firewall.

questions.q: A small branch office has a single FTD device and no central management server. The administrator wants to configure it by pointing a browser at the firewall itself. Which tool should be used?

choices.why: The FMC is a central manager recommended for multiple appliances, not an on-box manager.
CDO is a cloud-based manager for many devices, not a web manager running on the firewall.
Correct. FDM is the on-box web manager for small FTD deployments; you point a browser at the firewall.
FCM is the FXOS web GUI for chassis functions, not the manager for FTD security policies.

questions.q: An organization wants to manage its ASA, FTD, and Meraki security devices, plus virtual firewalls in AWS, from a cloud-based service that lets it write a policy once and enforce it everywhere. Which solution fits?

choices.why: Correct. CDO is a cloud-based manager for ASA, FTD, Meraki security devices, and AWS virtual firewalls, with central policy and templates.
ASDM is the ASA's GUI manager; it is not cloud-based and does not manage Meraki devices.
The Migration Tool converts ASA, FDM, and third-party configurations to Threat Defense; it does not manage devices.
Threat Response is an incident response hub for investigations, not a firewall policy manager.

questions.q: Which ASA models cannot run the FTD software?

choices.why: FTD runs natively on the ASA 5506-X and 5508-X.
FTD runs natively on the ASA 5525-X and 5545-X.
FTD runs natively on the ASA 5516-X and 5555-X.
Correct. FTD is not supported on the ASA 5505 or the 5585-X.

questions.q: On a router running ZBFW, interface G0/0 is in zone INSIDE and interface G0/2 is not assigned to any zone. What happens to traffic between G0/0 and G0/2?

choices.text: It flows freely because G0/2 has no zone restrictions
choices.why: Traffic flows freely only between interfaces in the same zone; a non-member interface cannot exchange traffic with a zone member.

choices.text: It is inspected by the self zone
choices.why: The self zone covers traffic to the router itself, not traffic between a zone member and a non-member interface.

choices.text: It cannot flow between the zone member and the non-member interface
choices.why: Correct. With ZBFW, traffic cannot flow between an interface in a zone and an interface that is not a zone member.

choices.text: It is allowed only if a zone pair applies a pass action
choices.why: Zone pairs and pass, inspect, and drop actions apply only between two zones, and G0/2 is not in a zone.

questions.section: 2. Comparing Network Security Solutions That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: In a Cisco SD-WAN zone-based firewall policy, what action can be taken on flows that match an application?

choices.text: They can be accepted and inspected
choices.why: Accept with inspect applies to matches on prefixes, ports, and protocols, not to application matches.
Correct. In the SD-WAN firewall policy, flows matching applications can only be denied.

choices.text: They can be passed without header inspection
choices.why: Pass is an option for accepted flows that match prefixes, ports, or protocols, not application matches.

choices.text: They are redirected to the self zone
choices.why: The self zone controls traffic to and from the device itself; it is not an action for application matches.

questions.section: 2. Comparing Network Security Solutions That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: A company wants to insert a firewall between its LAN and the next-hop router without changing any IP addresses on its hosts or router. Which firewall mode should it use?

choices.why: A routed firewall acts as an extra hop and needs a new network segment, which means planning, downtime, and readdressing.
Multiple context mode partitions the device into virtual firewalls; it doesn't by itself avoid readdressing.
Passive mode only inspects copied traffic from a SPAN or tap and doesn't sit in the path as a firewall.
Correct. A transparent (Layer 2) firewall bridges a pair of interfaces in the same subnet and goes between the LAN and router without readdressing.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: Why does a single-mode transparent ASA (SMTF) need a global management IP address?

choices.text: For Telnet and SSH management, and to source ARP requests and syslog
choices.why: Correct. The bridged interfaces have no IP addresses, so a global management IP is used for Telnet and SSH and to source ARP and syslog.

choices.text: To route traffic between the inside and outside subnets
choices.why: A transparent firewall bridges a single subnet; it doesn't route between subnets.

choices.text: To act as the default gateway for inside hosts
choices.why: Inside hosts still use the next-hop router as their default gateway; the transparent firewall is invisible to them.

choices.text: To form a dynamic routing adjacency with the next-hop router
choices.why: An SMTF uses no dynamic routing; its setup is only ACLs, inspection rules, and optional NAT.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: Which statement about Secure Firewall inline sets is correct?

choices.text: They can be built on VLAN subinterfaces
choices.why: Inline sets can't use VLANs; they work only on physical interfaces and EtherChannels.

choices.text: They support NAT, routing, and full ASA ACLs
choices.why: Most legacy ASA features such as NAT, routing, and ACLs are not available on an inline pair.
Correct. Inline sets work only on physical interfaces and EtherChannels and can't use redundant interfaces or VLANs.

choices.text: They do not work with clustering
choices.why: Inline sets and passive interfaces work with both intra-chassis and inter-chassis clustering.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: Routers on either side of an FTD inline set run BFD, but BFD echo packets keep getting dropped. Why?

choices.text: BFD is a UDP protocol and needs an ACL for return traffic
choices.why: UDP return traffic is allowed automatically; the drop is specific to how inline sets treat BFD echo packets.

choices.text: Inline sets block all routing protocols by default
choices.why: Inline sets retransmit all traffic unless it is explicitly dropped; there is no default block of routing protocols.

choices.text: The FTD randomizes the TCP sequence numbers of BFD packets
choices.why: Sequence randomization affects TCP sessions like BGP MD5; it is not the reason BFD echo is dropped.

choices.text: BFD echo packets have the same source and destination IP address
choices.why: Correct. FTD drops BFD echo packets on inline sets because they have the same source and destination IP address.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: For best performance in a failover pair, what latency should the stateful failover link have?

choices.text: Less than 1 millisecond, and no more than 10 milliseconds
choices.why: These are tighter than the documented values; 10 ms is the best-performance target, and up to 250 ms is still allowed.

choices.text: Less than 10 milliseconds, and no more than 250 milliseconds
choices.why: Correct. State link latency should be under 10 ms for best performance and must not exceed 250 ms.

choices.text: Less than 100 milliseconds, and no more than 500 milliseconds
choices.why: These values are too loose; the state link should be under 10 ms for best performance and never over 250 ms.

choices.text: Less than 30 milliseconds, and no more than 1 second
choices.why: These values are not the documented targets; the state link should be under 10 ms and at most 250 ms, not up to a full second.

questions.q: On which platforms does Cisco support Secure Firewall clustering?

choices.why: Correct. Clustering is supported on the Firepower 9300 and 4100 series, with intra-chassis clustering on the 9300 backplane.
These smaller models are for branch offices and are not the listed clustering platforms.
The ISA3000 is a rugged industrial appliance and Threat Defense Virtual is the virtual FTD; neither is the listed clustering platform.
These are small ASA models that can run FTD, but they are not the listed clustering platforms.

questions.q: An engineer needs an ACL for an OSPF route map that matches only destination networks, where the source does not matter. Which ACL type should be used?

choices.why: An extended ACL matches source and destination, protocols, and ports; it is used for interface filtering, not where only the destination matters.
A Webtype ACL restricts traffic through SSL VPN tunnels.
An EtherType ACL filters on Layer 2 Ethernet type codes in transparent mode.
Correct. A standard ACL matches only destination IP addresses and is used by processes such as route maps, OSPF, and split tunneling.

questions.q: An ASA must allow 3 outside hosts to reach 2 internal servers using 2 services. Without object grouping, how many ACEs are needed?

choices.why: Adding the numbers (3 + 2 + 2) gives 7, but each combination needs its own ACE, so the counts are multiplied.
6 covers only hosts times servers; each pair also needs one ACE per service.
Correct. 2 servers times 3 hosts times 2 services equals 12 ACEs without object grouping.
With object grouping the viewable list collapses to one entry, but the question asks without grouping, and the real ACE count doesn't change anyway.

questions.q: Which keyword on the access-group command turns an ACL into a management access rule that filters traffic destined to the ASA itself?

choices.why: The global keyword applies an ACL to inbound traffic on all interfaces for through-the-box traffic, not to-the-box traffic.
Correct. Applying the ACL with the control-plane keyword makes it a to-the-box management access rule.
log is added to an ACE to generate logs for matches; it does not change what traffic the ACL applies to.
inter-interface is part of the same-security-traffic command, not an access-group keyword.

questions.q: An ASA has a control-plane ACL denying all IP traffic on the outside interface, but host 10.2.2.2 is allowed by the ssh command. Can 10.2.2.2 still open an SSH session to the ASA?

choices.text: No, because the control-plane ACL denies all IP
choices.why: Management protocols' own lists take precedence over management access rules, so the ssh command wins.

choices.text: No, because SSH needs an extended ACL on the inside interface
choices.why: SSH access to the ASA is controlled by the ssh command list, not by an inside interface ACL.

choices.text: Only if the ASA is in multiple context mode
choices.why: Context mode does not change this precedence; the ssh command list wins in either mode.

choices.text: Yes, because the ssh command takes precedence over the management access rule
choices.why: Correct. A host allowed by the ssh command can still SSH in even if a management access rule blocks it.

questions.q: Hosts already use NAT to reach the Internet, but traffic to one specific partner network must not be translated. Which NAT type should be used?

choices.why: Correct. Identity NAT bypasses translation so the address stays the same, used when hosts shouldn't be translated to a specific host or network.
Static NAT creates a fixed one-to-one translation to a different address, which is still a translation.
Extended PAT allows 65,535 translations per service instead of per address; it still translates.
Outside NAT translates outside hosts going to a higher-security interface; it does not exempt inside traffic.

questions.q: Which Secure Firewall preprocessor watches DCE/RPC and SMB traffic for anomalies and evasions?

choices.why: The Sun RPC preprocessor normalizes and reassembles fragmented SunRPC records; it does not handle SMB.
Correct. The DCE/RPC preprocessor monitors DCE/RPC and SMB for anomalies and evasions.
The SIP preprocessor extracts SIP header and body and alerts on out-of-order calls and anomalies.
The GTP preprocessor normalizes GTP command channel signaling.

questions.q: Malware authors change a file slightly to evade hash matching, but its structure stays the same. Which Secure Malware Defense engine is designed to catch these polymorphic variants?

choices.why: 1-to-1 signatures compare exact hashes, so any file change evades them.
Dynamic analysis runs the sample in Malware Analytics; it is not the fingerprinting engine for polymorphic variants.
Advanced analytics ranks executed files by how common they are to find rare threats; it does not fingerprint file structure.
Correct. Ethos is the fuzzy fingerprinting engine using static or passive heuristics, built on the idea that structure often stays the same when content changes.

questions.q: A host's IP address is on a Security Intelligence allowlist. How does Secure Firewall treat its traffic?

choices.text: It is trusted and fast-pathed past all further inspection
choices.why: An allowlist does not trust or fast-path traffic; that would be a Trust rule action, not Security Intelligence.

choices.text: It is exempted from the blocklist but still goes through the rest of access control
choices.why: Correct. The allowlist exempts traffic from the blocklist only; allowlisted traffic is still evaluated by the rest of access control.
Watching matches without blocking is a monitor-only blocklist, and the allowlist does not block.

choices.text: It is sent to Malware Analytics for sandboxing
choices.why: Sandboxing applies to files under a file policy; an allowlist entry doesn't send traffic to the sandbox.

questions.section: 8. Security Intelligence, Security Updates, and Keeping Firepower Software Up to Date

questions.q: Cisco uses two capitalizations of the same brand. What does "FirePOWER" with uppercase POWER refer to?

choices.text: The FTD unified image and newer software
choices.why: That is "Firepower" with lowercase power. Uppercase FirePOWER refers to the older ASA module.

choices.text: The operating system on Firepower chassis
choices.why: The chassis operating system is FXOS (Firepower eXtensible Operating System).

choices.text: The Cisco ASA FirePOWER Services module
choices.why: Correct. FirePOWER with uppercase POWER is the name for the ASA FirePOWER Services module that brought Sourcefire technology into the ASA.
That is Cisco Secure Firewall Cloud Native, whose firewall component is the CNFW.

questions.q: A DevOps team wants to configure Cisco Secure Firewall Cloud Native as infrastructure as code. What do they use to configure it?

choices.text: The FXOS CLI and Firepower Chassis Manager
choices.why: The FXOS CLI and FCM configure physical Firepower chassis functions, not Cloud Native.

choices.text: K8s REST APIs and YAML files
choices.why: Correct. Secure Firewall Cloud Native is configured with Kubernetes REST APIs and YAML files, an IaC approach.
ASDM and the ASA CLI manage ASA appliances, not the Kubernetes-based Cloud Native firewall.

choices.text: The Device Setup Wizard in FDM
choices.why: The Device Setup Wizard is for the initial setup of an FTD device managed by FDM.

cards: K8s REST APIs and YAML files

questions.q: A company's public website is being targeted with SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and advanced bots that mimic human behavior. Which Cisco solution addresses this best?

choices.text: Cisco Secure WAF and bot protection
choices.why: Correct. Cisco Secure WAF protects websites, applications, and APIs against exploits such as SQL injection and XSS, and also defends against advanced bots.
The ISA3000 is a rugged industrial appliance for OT networks, not a web application firewall.
ZBFW is a stateful router firewall based on zones; it does not specialize in web application exploits or bots.
The ASA uses this database to block traffic to and from botnets, not to protect a website against SQL injection or bots mimicking humans.

cards: Cisco Secure WAF and bot protection

questions.q: On which ASA models can FirePOWER Services be managed with ASDM and their licenses installed with ASDM?

choices.why: These models don't run FTD, and they are not the models listed for ASDM management of FirePOWER Services.
On these models the licenses are installed in the FirePOWER module, not through ASDM.
These are Firepower chassis platforms that run FTD logical devices, not ASA models with a FirePOWER module.
Correct. On the 5506-X, 5508-X, and 5516-X, FirePOWER Services can be managed with ASDM and licenses installed with ASDM.

questions.q: Cisco IOS Zone-Based Firewall replaced which legacy IOS firewall feature?

choices.why: MPF is the ASA framework for application inspection and QoS, not a legacy IOS firewall.
Correct. ZBFW replaced CBAC and added features CBAC lacks, such as assigning interfaces to zones.
PIX was a standalone Cisco firewall appliance before the ASA, not an IOS feature.
TCP Intercept protects servers from SYN floods; it is not the legacy IOS firewall ZBFW replaced.

questions.section: 2. Comparing Network Security Solutions That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: In a Cisco SD-WAN zone-based firewall, what is the difference between inspecting and passing an accepted flow?

choices.text: Inspect sends the flow to the IPS; pass sends it to URL filtering
choices.why: Inspect and pass describe header handling in the firewall policy, not handoffs to other security engines.

choices.text: Inspect drops the flow and logs it; pass forwards it
choices.why: Inspect does not drop the flow; drop is a separate action for matching flows.

choices.text: Inspect checks the header for source address and port; pass sends the flow on with no header inspection
choices.why: Correct. An inspected flow has its header checked for source address and port, while a passed flow is sent on without header inspection.

choices.text: Inspect is for applications; pass is for IP prefixes only
choices.why: Application matches can only be denied; inspect and pass apply to accepted flows matched on prefixes, ports, and protocols.

questions.section: 2. Comparing Network Security Solutions That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: Which statement about ASA security contexts is correct?

choices.text: The firewall mode, routed or transparent, can be set per context
choices.why: Correct. In multiple context mode, each context can be set to routed or transparent mode.

choices.text: All contexts must share one routing table
choices.why: Each security context has its own configuration, interfaces, policies, routing table, and administrators.

choices.text: The admin context can be created after the user contexts
choices.why: The admin context must be created before other contexts and must be on the local disk.

choices.text: Contexts cannot be used when networks overlap
choices.why: Connecting overlapping networks without readdressing is one of the listed use cases for security contexts.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: Which is a requirement of an ASA multimode transparent firewall (MMTF) that does not apply to a single-mode transparent firewall?

choices.text: Each interface must be in a separate failover group
choices.why: Failover groups are not part of the MMTF requirements described for transparent contexts.

choices.text: The ASA must run dynamic routing in every context
choices.why: Transparent firewalls bridge traffic; dynamic routing is not a requirement for MMTF.

choices.text: All contexts must share the same inside interface
choices.why: The opposite is true: in MMTF, interfaces can't be shared between contexts.

choices.text: Each context needs an IP address on its BVI for management
choices.why: Correct. In multimode transparent firewalls, each context needs an IP on its BVI for management, and interfaces can't be shared.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: An engineer wants an FTD to inspect a copy of traffic with full Snort checks while the device is physically cabled in the traffic path, so it can later be switched to blocking. Which interface mode fits?

choices.why: Passive with ERSPAN receives traffic through a GRE tunnel from a remote capture point; it is not cabled in the path.
Correct. Inline pair with tap bridges two physical interfaces in the path but runs firewall and Snort checks on a copy of the traffic.
A routed interface acts as a Layer 3 hop and enforces policy on the real traffic, not a copy.
A standard inline pair inspects and can drop the actual traffic, rather than inspecting a copy.

questions.section: 3. Deployment Modes of Network Security Solutions and Architectures That Provide Firewall Capabilities

questions.q: Which interface can be used as an FTD failover link?

choices.text: A physical, redundant, or EtherChannel interface not otherwise used
choices.why: Correct. The failover link can be a physical, redundant, or EtherChannel interface not used for anything else.

choices.text: A VLAN subinterface of the inside interface
choices.why: Subinterfaces are not supported for failover links, and named interfaces like inside can't be used.
The failover link can't be an interface that is already named, such as outside, inside, or dmz-1.

choices.text: The same interface used for the state link and data traffic
choices.why: Failover and state interfaces can be used only for that purpose, and separate interfaces are recommended for each.

questions.q: Two FTD units are connected for failover by a direct Ethernet cable. Why does Cisco list this as harder to troubleshoot than using a switch?

choices.text: Direct cables don't support stateful failover
choices.why: A direct cable can carry failover and state traffic; the issue is identifying which unit failed.

choices.text: A direct cable requires DHCP on the failover interfaces
choices.why: DHCP is not supported on a failover pair at all, whether the link uses a switch or not.

choices.text: A direct cable forces Active-Active failover
choices.why: Cabling does not change the failover mode; Secure Firewall supports only Active-Standby.

choices.text: An interface failure takes the link down on both peers, so it is hard to tell which unit failed
choices.why: Correct. Without a switch, one interface failure brings the link down on both units, which makes it difficult to find the failed unit.

questions.q: In a Secure Firewall cluster, where should an administrator make configuration changes?

choices.text: On any slave unit, which forwards changes to the master
choices.why: Configuration is not done on slave units; it is done on the master and replicated outward.

choices.text: On the master unit, which replicates them to the other members
choices.why: Correct. All configuration is done on the master, which replicates it to the other cluster members.

choices.text: On each unit separately, then synced by FCM
choices.why: Members share the security policy through replication from the master, not by separate per-unit configuration.

choices.text: On the chassis supervisor's bootstrap configuration
choices.why: The supervisor pushes only a minimal bootstrap with the cluster name and cluster control link settings, not the full configuration.

questions.q: How many access lists can be bound to one direction of a single ASA interface at the same time?

choices.text: Only one ACL of any type
choices.why: An EtherType ACL can be bound together with an extended ACL, so it is not limited to one ACL in total.

choices.text: Two extended ACLs and one EtherType ACL
choices.why: Only one extended ACL per direction is allowed.

choices.text: One extended ACL and one EtherType ACL
choices.why: Correct. One extended ACL and one EtherType ACL can be bound in each direction of an interface at the same time.

choices.text: Unlimited, evaluated in the order applied
choices.why: The number is limited to one extended and one EtherType ACL per direction.

questions.q: An ASA allows outbound traffic from inside hosts. Users report that GRE tunnels and IPsec ESP traffic fail, while TCP and UDP applications work. What is the most likely reason?

choices.text: Connectionless protocols like GRE and ESP need their return traffic permitted in the ACL
choices.why: Correct. TCP and UDP return traffic is allowed automatically, but GRE, ESP, and other connectionless protocols need return traffic permitted.

choices.text: GRE and ESP are blocked by the self zone
choices.why: The self zone is a ZBFW concept on IOS routers, not an ASA mechanism.

choices.text: GRE and ESP require static PAT
choices.why: GRE has no Layer 4 port information, so it uses dynamic NAT, not port-based translation.

choices.text: TCP Intercept is dropping GRE and ESP packets
choices.why: TCP Intercept protects TCP servers from SYN floods; it doesn't affect GRE or ESP.

questions.q: Which ASA ACL type restricts traffic coming through SSL VPN tunnels?

choices.why: A standard ACL matches destination addresses for processes such as split tunneling and route maps; it is not the SSL VPN filtering ACL.
An EtherType ACL filters Layer 2 Ethernet type codes in transparent mode.
A global ACL applies to inbound traffic on every interface, not specifically to SSL VPN traffic.
Correct. A Webtype ACL restricts traffic through SSL VPN tunnels. If one is defined and nothing matches, the packet is dropped.

questions.q: An organization hosts web, email, DNS, and FTP servers that outside users must reach at fixed public addresses. Which translation method is recommended?

choices.why: Dynamic PAT shares one address among many hosts for outbound connections, so it doesn't give servers fixed public addresses.
Correct. Static NAT is a fixed one-to-one translation and is recommended for servers offering email, web, DNS, and FTP to outside users.
Dynamic NAT assigns addresses from a pool, so a server's public address isn't fixed.
Policy PAT translates only packets that match an ACL or manual NAT rule; it is not the general recommendation for public servers.

questions.q: An engineer must write a NAT rule that translates a host's source address only when it talks to one particular destination network. Which kind of NAT rule is required?

choices.why: Auto NAT is defined in a network object and translates the source regardless of destination, so it can't take the destination into account.
Extended PAT changes how many PAT translations are available per service; it doesn't add destination matching.
Correct. Manual NAT is needed for rules that involve destination addresses, such as policy NAT, or for translating both source and destination.
Static PAT redirects ports on one global IP to inside servers; it doesn't make translation depend on the destination.

questions.q: What is the role of a network analysis policy in Secure Firewall?

choices.text: It governs how traffic is decoded and preprocessed for further evaluation
choices.why: Correct. The network analysis policy handles decoding and preprocessing, which happens before and separately from intrusion rule inspection.

choices.text: It uses intrusion rules to examine decoded packets for attack patterns
choices.why: That describes an intrusion policy, which is paired with variable sets and runs after network analysis.

choices.text: It passively discovers hosts and applications without affecting traffic
choices.why: That describes the network discovery policy, the only policy that can't affect traffic.

choices.text: It blocks IPs, URLs, and domains by reputation before deeper inspection
choices.why: That describes Security Intelligence, which runs early in access control.

questions.q: Which group maintains the official rule sets of Snort.org, ClamAV, SenderBase.org, and SpamCop?

choices.why: OASIS maintains the STIX and TAXII threat intelligence standards, not Snort or ClamAV rule sets.
MITRE developed STIX and TAXII; it does not maintain these rule sets.
Immunet is an AV community that contributes data; it doesn't maintain the official rule sets.
Correct. Talos maintains the official rule sets of Snort.org, ClamAV, SenderBase.org, and SpamCop, using data from malware samples, the web, and email.

cards: Cisco Talos (Talos Security Intelligence and Research Group)

questions.q: A security team wants an open, automated way to transport threat indicators between its tools and partners. Which standard provides this transport?

choices.why: STIX is the format for describing threat intelligence; TAXII is the transport used to exchange it.
Correct. TAXII (Trusted Automated eXchange of Indicator Information) is an open transport for automated exchange of threat information, maintained by OASIS.
GTP is the GPRS Tunneling Protocol used in mobile networks, not a threat intelligence transport.
CIP (Common Industrial Protocol) is an industrial Ethernet protocol, not a threat sharing standard.

cards: TAXII (Trusted Automated eXchange of Indicator Information)

questions.q: Starting with which ASA software version can a single ACL filter both IPv4 and IPv6 traffic?

choices.why: 8.2(1) predates unified ACLs; the first version where one ACL filters both IPv4 and IPv6 is 9.0(1).
8.4(2) is not the documented version; unified IPv4 and IPv6 ACLs arrived in 9.0(1).
Correct. ASA 9.0(1) is the first version where one ACL can filter both IPv4 and IPv6.
9.8(1) is later than the version that introduced the feature, which was 9.0(1).

questions.q: A company is replacing its Palo Alto Networks and Check Point firewalls with Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense. Which tool converts the existing configurations?

choices.why: Correct. The Migration Tool converts ASA, FDM, and third-party configurations such as Check Point, Palo Alto Networks, and Fortinet to Threat Defense.

choices.text: Cisco ASA to Threat Defense Feature Mapping guide
choices.why: The Feature Mapping guide only maps ASA features to their Threat Defense equivalents; it does not convert configurations.
CDO manages and enforces policies across devices from the cloud; the Migration Tool is the product for converting third-party configurations.
A platform settings policy applies shared parameters like time and external authentication to many devices; it does not migrate configurations.

questions.q: After a malware outbreak, an analyst needs to see which hosts and users transferred a malicious file, which hosts are at risk, and whether the transfers were blocked. Which FMC feature shows this?

choices.why: The Summary Dashboard shows top attackers, top targets, intrusion events, and events by application protocol, not a file's transfer path.
Correct. Network File Trajectory maps file transfers across hosts, the file's disposition, and whether transfers were blocked or files quarantined.
Variable sets hold named network and port values for intrusion rules; they show no file data.
A platform settings policy applies shared device parameters; it is not an analysis feature.

questions.q: A SOC wants a platform that automates repetitive security operations tasks such as incident response playbooks, threat hunting, and vulnerability management across many integrated tools. Which category of solution is this?

choices.why: A SIEM aggregates and correlates event data for detection, investigation, and compliance reporting; automating workflows is the focus of SOAR.
An IDS detects attacks and generates alerts; it does not orchestrate operations tasks across tools.
A WAF protects web applications from exploits like SQL injection and XSS; it is not an operations automation platform.
Correct. SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response) automates and orchestrates tasks such as incident response, threat hunting, and vulnerability management.

questions.q: An analyst adds a third-party EDR product to Cisco SecureX, but none of its data or response actions appear. What must be done first?

choices.text: Register the product with the FMC using a registration key
choices.why: Registration keys authenticate managed devices to the FMC; they don't connect products to SecureX.
Committing applies intrusion policy changes in the FMC; it has nothing to do with SecureX data sources.

choices.text: Configure an integration module for that product
choices.why: Correct. A SecureX integration module must be configured before that product's data and response actions appear.

choices.text: Add the product to a security zone
choices.why: Security zones group firewall interfaces for policy matching; they do not link products to SecureX.

questions.q: An attacker launches an exploit against a Windows server that is already patched for that vulnerability. Which NGIPS capability lets the system recognize that the event has low impact?

choices.why: Correct. NGIPS impact assessment uses host vulnerability context, so it knows a patched system can't be severely impacted by that exploit.
Pattern matching is what legacy IPS relies on; it fires on the attempt without knowing whether the target is vulnerable.
Fail-open lets traffic bypass a failed inline device; it is not an event assessment capability.
Passive mode is an interface deployment option for monitoring copies of traffic, not a way to assess event impact.

questions.q: In the attack continuum model of before, during, and after an attack, in which phase does an NGIPS mostly operate?

choices.why: The before phase is about controls such as access policy and hardening; the NGIPS works mainly while attacks are happening.
The after phase is covered by capabilities such as retrospection and file trajectory, not mainly by the NGIPS.
Recovery is not one of the three attack continuum phases, which are before, during, and after.
Correct. The NGIPS works mostly in the during phase of the attack continuum.

questions.q: When an FTD device in an inline deployment is registered to the FMC, which security zones are created automatically?

choices.why: These are common ASA interface names, not the zones FTD creates at registration.
Correct. FTD creates zones based on detection mode: External and Internal zones for inline deployments, and a passive zone for passive deployments.
A passive zone is created for passive deployments, not inline ones.

choices.text: A self zone and a default zone
choices.why: The self zone is a ZBFW concept on IOS routers, and a default zone tied to a VPN is used in SD-WAN.

questions.q: An engineer creates an FMC access control rule to block Telnet and wants the firewall to send a TCP reset to the client instead of silently dropping the connection. Which action should be selected?

choices.why: Monitor logs matching traffic and lets evaluation continue; it does not block or reset.
Interactive block is one of the four block actions, but it does not send a reset; the reset variants are block with reset and interactive block with reset.
Correct. Block with reset blocks the connection and sends a reset, as in the book's Block Telnet Rule for TCP port 23.
Trust passes traffic without further inspection, the opposite of blocking.

questions.q: An administrator moves an access control rule into a new section and category in the FMC. How does this affect rule evaluation?

choices.text: Rules in a named category are evaluated before uncategorized rules
choices.why: Categories don't create priority; evaluation follows the rule numbers.

choices.text: The rule becomes a Monitor rule until redeployed
choices.why: Moving a rule doesn't change its action.

choices.text: The rule is evaluated last, after the default action
choices.why: The default action applies only when no rule matches; sections and categories don't move rules after it.

choices.text: It doesn't, because sections and categories are only organizational
choices.why: Correct. Sections and categories are only organizational and don't change rule position.

questions.q: In an inline Secure Firewall deployment, which policy cannot drop or modify traffic?

choices.why: Correct. The network discovery policy is passive, so it is the only policy that can't affect traffic.
Security Intelligence can drop traffic early by reputation.
The SSL policy is one of the listed policies that can drop or modify traffic in inline deployments.
File policies can block files in inline deployments.

questions.q: An administrator edits an intrusion policy in the FMC but leaves the page without committing. What is true?

choices.text: The changes are lost when leaving the page
choices.why: Leaving with uncommitted changes doesn't lose them; they wait until you commit or discard them.

choices.text: The changes take effect immediately on all devices
choices.why: A policy doesn't take effect until the changes are committed.

choices.text: The changes are kept, but the policy doesn't take effect until committed
choices.why: Correct. Uncommitted changes are kept, and the policy takes effect only after commit. You can also discard changes since the last commit.

choices.text: The FMC commits the changes automatically after a validation check
choices.why: The validation check runs after a commit that you perform; the FMC does not commit for you.

questions.q: In a Secure Firewall port variable, what does the value [1024-] mean?

choices.why: Ports less than a number are written with a leading dash, such as [-1024].
Correct. A trailing dash, as in [1024-], means ports more than that number.
Excluding a port uses an exclamation point, such as [!25].
A single port is written as just the number; the trailing dash makes it an open-ended range.

questions.q: An organization manages 40 FTD devices and wants to apply the same time and date settings and external authentication to all of them at once. What should it use?

choices.why: Variable sets hold network and port variables for intrusion policies, not device parameters like time or authentication.
A network analysis policy governs decoding and preprocessing of traffic, not device settings.
The cluster control link connects cluster members; it does not distribute settings to independent devices.
Correct. A platform settings policy is a shared set of device parameters, such as time and external authentication, applied to many devices at once.

questions.q: What does extended PAT change compared with standard PAT?

choices.text: It allows 65,535 translations per service instead of per address
choices.why: Correct. Extended PAT provides 65,535 PAT translations per service instead of per address.

choices.text: It translates both source and destination addresses
choices.why: That describes bidirectional NAT, or manual NAT translating both addresses.

choices.text: It maps one port on a global IP to an inside server
choices.why: That describes static PAT, also called port redirection.

choices.text: It keeps the address unchanged and bypasses translation
choices.why: That describes identity NAT.

questions.q: When an ACL is applied outbound on an ASA interface, what happens to a packet before the ACEs are checked?

choices.text: Nothing; outbound ACLs are checked before any other processing
choices.why: That describes an inbound ACL, where packets are checked on arrival.

choices.text: It is checked against the global ACL
choices.why: A global ACL applies to inbound traffic on every interface; it is not the step before an outbound ACL.

choices.text: It goes through NAT, QoS, and VPN processing first
choices.why: Correct. With an outbound ACL, packets go through NAT, QoS, and VPN before the ACEs are checked and the packet leaves.

choices.text: It is sent to the Firepower engine for Snort inspection
choices.why: Snort inspection belongs to Secure Firewall's Firepower engine, not ASA outbound ACL processing.

questions.q: A web server behind an ASA is being hit by a SYN flood DoS attack. Which ASA feature, configured with MPF connection limits, protects it?

choices.why: The Botnet Traffic Filter blocks traffic based on an external botnet database; it is not the SYN flood protection configured with MPF.
A time-based ACL applies only during a time range; it does not protect against SYN floods.
Identity NAT bypasses address translation; it offers no DoS protection.
Correct. TCP Intercept protects TCP servers from SYN flood DoS attacks and is configured with MPF connection limits.

questions.q: An ASA has both an ICMP policy (icmp commands) and a control-plane ACL applied to the outside interface. Which one takes precedence for ICMP sent to the ASA?

choices.why: Correct. ICMP filtering takes precedence over control-plane filtering.
The control-plane ACL filters to-the-box traffic, but ICMP filtering takes precedence over it.

choices.text: The interface ACL applied with access-group
choices.why: Interface ACLs that block ICMP don't block ICMP to the ASA's own interface by default.
A global ACL filters through-the-box traffic on all interfaces, not ICMP destined to the ASA.

questions.q: Which Cisco Secure Malware Analytics tool lets an analyst interact with a malware sample and troubleshoot it during analysis?

choices.why: Spero is the Secure Malware Defense machine-learning engine, not an interactive analysis tool.
Correct. Glovebox is the Malware Analytics tool for interacting with malware and troubleshooting.
Network File Trajectory is an FMC feature showing how files moved across hosts; it doesn't let you interact with samples.
The Graph panel in SecureX Threat Response shows observables and relationships; it is not a sample interaction tool.

questions.q: Which Secure Malware Defense capability provides a kernel-level view of network I/O and traces it back to the process that started it?

choices.why: Advanced analytics uses big data to rank executed files from least to most common; it doesn't trace network I/O to a process.
IOCs are artifacts that indicate an intrusion, such as FileItem or RegistryItem entries; they are not a network I/O monitor.
Correct. Device flow correlation gives a kernel-level view of network I/O traced back to the originating process, and can block or alert on it.
1-to-1 signatures compare file hashes against a database; they don't monitor network activity.
